No. The land-change method could not evaluate ASSET-J. The source coverage this asset needs had not been prepared, so no observation was made. Hansen GFC, JRC GFC2020 and MGAP 2021 were all unavailable for it.

The result is "insufficient evidence because of missing coverage" for tree-cover loss across the whole asset boundary from 2021-01-01 to 2025-12-31, against the 2020-12-31 baseline.

This does not tell you whether tree-cover loss occurred. It doesn't show that no loss occurred, and it makes no regulatory or compliance finding, such as EUDR compliant, non-compliant or deforestation-free.

To get an answer, the missing source coverage would have to be prepared and the assessment rerun. This evidence is current as of 2026-11-12.
